questionText:
Consider a network with three routers P, Q, R shown in the figure below. All the links have cost of unity.

The routers exchange distance vector routing information and have converged on the routing tables, after which the link Q–R fails. Assume that P and Q send out routing updates at random times, each at the same average rate. The probability of a routing loop formation (rounded off to one decimal place) between P and Q, leading to count-to-infinity problem, is ____________.
explanation:
Step 1: Initial State before Failure
Initially, the network has converged:
• $Q$ reaches $R$ directly with cost $1$.
• $P$ reaches $R$ via $Q$ with cost $1 + 1 = 2$.

Step 2: Link Failure and Loop Formation Condition
When link $Q-R$ fails:
• If $P$ sends its routing update to $Q$ first (before $Q$ sends its update to $P$), $P$ advertises its route to $R$ with cost $2$. Router $Q$ updates its table to route to $R$ through $P$ with cost $2 + 1 = 3$. This creates a routing loop between $P$ and $Q$ leading to the count-to-infinity problem.
• If $Q$ sends its routing update to $P$ first, $P$ recognizes that $R$ is no longer reachable through $Q$, preventing the loop.

Step 3: Calculating Probability
Since $P$ and $Q$ transmit routing updates independently at random times with the same average rate, the probability that $P$ transmits before $Q$ is:
$$P = \frac{1}{2} = 0.5$$

Hence, the probability of a routing loop formation is 0.5.
